question.prompt: Sides \(AB,\) \(BC,\) \(CD,\) and \(DA,\) respectively, of convex quadrilateral \(ABCD\) are extended past \(B,\) \(C,\) \(D,\) and \(A\) to points \(B',\) \(C',\) \(D',\) and \(A'.\) Also, \(AB=BB'=6,\) \(BC=CC'=7,\) \(CD=DD'=8,\) and \(DA=AA'=9;\) and the area of \(ABCD\) is \(10.\) The area of \(A'B'C'D'\) is

solutions.explanation:
The equal extensions let us compare triangle areas without finding any angles. Write \([PQR]\) for the area of triangle \(PQR\), and let \(S=10\) be the area of \(ABCD\).

The enlarged quadrilateral consists of \(ABCD\) and the four triangles \(AA'B'\), \(BB'C'\), \(CC'D'\), and \(DD'A'\). These pieces have disjoint interiors: convexity places each added triangle outside an original side, adjacent added triangles are separated by an original side line, and the opposite pairs are separated by diagonals \(AC\) and \(BD\). Tracing the remaining edges gives boundary \(A'B'C'D'\).

Consider triangle \(AA'B'\). The equal segments \(AA'\) and \(AD\) lie on the same line, so triangles \(AA'B'\) and \(DAB'\) have equal bases and the same altitude from \(B'\). Hence their areas are equal. Also, \(AB'=2AB\), so triangles \(DAB'\) and \(DAB\) have base ratio \(2\) and the same altitude from \(D\). Therefore
\[
[AA'B']=[DAB']=2[DAB].
\]
The same comparison at the other vertices gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
[BB'C']&=2[ABC],\\
[CC'D']&=2[BCD],\\
[DD'A']&=2[CDA].
\end{aligned}
\]
Diagonal \(BD\) splits the original quadrilateral into triangles \(DAB\) and \(BCD\), while diagonal \(AC\) splits it into \(ABC\) and \(CDA\). Thus
\[
[DAB]+[BCD]=S,
\qquad
[ABC]+[CDA]=S.
\]
The four added triangles consequently have total area \(2(S+S)=4S\). The required area is
\[
S+4S=5\cdot10=\boxed{50},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
solutions.title: Compare the added triangle areas
